body: That is what I tried first and oddly enough, `kCFStringEncodingUTF32` is different from `kCFStringEncodingUTF32LE`, and didn't work. I would have thought `kCFStringEncodingUTF32` was defined to match the endianness of the platform (which it probably is internally), but they are different constants.
Good catch. I'll use `platform` instead.

> Generic Unix implementation is not waiting for completion

It is waiting, as that is what [`pclose`](https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man3/pclose.3p.html) does:

> The `pclose()` function shall close a stream that was opened by `popen()`, **wait for the command to terminate**, and return the termination status of the process that was running the command language interpreter.

Granted, we're reading from the pipe, after the process has terminated, but that shouldn't matter. What I am observing is that the current implementation is sometimes not capturing all the data, and because `**ARCHIVE SUCCEEDED**` is the last of the output, this line fails:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/99451a27e9e562815194a087f1d8592759fb072b/editor/export/editor_export_platform_apple_embedded.cpp#L2172

We could refactor `OS_Unix::execute` to use `feof`, `fread` and `ferror`, which is probably more robust, but I didn't want to potentially affect the other platforms for now.
…actually, the array is a better idea, as we'll also get Apple Watches with `platform: iOS`.

> It is waiting, as that is what [pclose](https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man3/pclose.3p.html) does

It's waiting only after reading is done, not before it. So if it's called from a thread, another thread can get partially read pipe data while the process is still running. ~But I'm not sure if it's actually used anywhere.~
Exposed GDScript wrapper only return when pipe is closed, so it can be used only internally.

Edit: `EditorNode::execute_and_show_output` seems to do it.
I'll remove this and the old Apple Embedded one too
